title: Toyonge (Red Creek)
summary: Toyonge is Red Creek at the head of Peconic Bay in Southampton.
history_content: Paucamp's 1660 testimony identified Toyoungs as one of the western Peconic Bay creeks and a boundary place. The same creek was also called Mashmanock in a 1648 deed, a relationship that still needs local map review.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Toyoungs, Toyonge, Toyoung, Toyongs, and Toyong. The name is interpreted as a ford or wading place.

Why Place Names Matter

“When your community begins to refer to local places and sites by their traditional name, that language name then becomes revitalised and any significant stories and history associated with the traditional name are restored to the identity of the site.”

— First Languages Australia, Councils engaging with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages (n.d.), Place naming and dual naming of local sites
preservation_content: Toyonge preserves the wading-place geography of Red Creek and the west-end Peconic Bay boundary landscape remembered in Shinnecock and colonial records.
